project_folder: Design Phase for Project Id PZSYVHVX

verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 5, 7, 8, 10: orange/terracotta trapezoidal-profile metal sheet roof with regular ribs; page 19 shows a tape measuring the sheet profile pitch (0.20 m).
verdicts.rationale: Roof photos clearly show a profiled/corrugated metal sheet roof, matching the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Roof surface itself is clear of fixtures (pages 8, 10). However a large tree rises immediately behind the roof ridge and appears taller than the roof (pages 5, 10), and a yellow water tank sits on the adjacent concrete slab beside the roof edge (pages 5, 10; tank also modelled in layout on pages 17-18).
verdicts.rationale: No obstructions on the sheet surface, but the nearby tall tree and adjacent water tank could cast shade on the proposed array; distance/direction cannot be confirmed from photos.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Low-pitch gable sheet roof visible on pages 5, 7, 8, 10; slope appears shallow (roughly 8-12°). Panels will be flush-mounted on mini-rails so panel angle equals roof slope.
verdicts.rationale: Visual estimate of a shallow gable is consistent with 8°; exact degree cannot be measured from photos.

verdicts.question: In case of sloped roof, what is the slope angle of the roof? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Same gable sheet roof (pages 5, 8, 10) with a shallow pitch, visually roughly 8-12°.
verdicts.rationale: Shallow pitch visible in photos is consistent with the stated 8° roof slope.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Single gable sheet roof over the headroom (pages 5, 10); layout on pages 17-18 places 2 panels on one face and 3 on the other face of the same roof.
verdicts.rationale: One roof structure (two faces of one gable) is used, matching '1'.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Trapezoidal metal sheet roof with ~0.20 m rib pitch (page 19); report header lists Mounting Structure Type 'Sheet Roof'. No structure installed yet.
verdicts.rationale: Short rails / mini-rails are the appropriate mounting for a trapezoidal sheet roof; planned structure is consistent with the roof seen in photos.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Site layout (page 17, compass N pointing up) shows a gable with the ridge running east-west: 2 panels on the north face and 3 on the south face. Pages 17-18 3D views are consistent.
verdicts.rationale: Layout compass and gable geometry support panels on south and north faces; orientation taken from the layout rather than independently from site photos.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6 (bottom) and 7 (top) show a steel ladder from the terrace up to the headroom roof, with route marked; page 5/7 show the steel walkway at the top of the ladder.
verdicts.rationale: Ladder access to the sheet roof is clearly shown.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.designer_answer: The height of the building is G+2+headroom is approximately 12 meters
verdicts.photo_observation: Building exterior (pages 5, 19): ground floor behind gate/compound wall, two upper storeys (window floor and balcony floor), topped by a sheet-roofed terrace; headroom with the orange sheet roof is behind and seen from terrace photos (pages 6-7).
verdicts.rationale: Visible storey count is consistent with G+2+headroom (~12 m); the headroom itself is not clearly visible in the front elevation.

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Front elevation (pages 5, 19) shows a residential multi-storey house with a sheet canopy at top; roof photos show the corrugated sheet roof described.
verdicts.rationale: Site photos match the described residential building and sheet roof.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Several overhead conductors cross the street directly in front of the building at roof level (pages 5, 19). A lattice transmission tower is visible only in the far distance (page 7, top-right). Voltage class of the nearby lines cannot be determined from photos.
verdicts.rationale: Overhead lines are present within ~10 m in front of the building; they look like LT distribution/service lines but cannot be confirmed as non-HT from photos.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5/19: paved street directly in front of the main gate; material lifting route drawn from street level up the front facade.
verdicts.rationale: Road access to the gate is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The building Chajja are the obstacles that could affect the material lifting.
verdicts.photo_observation: Lifting route on page 5 runs up the front facade past projecting sunshades/chajjas, balcony slab and the top canopy overhang.
verdicts.rationale: Projecting chajjas along the lifting route are visible, consistent with the designer's note.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: The earth pits are located west side of the corridor which is near to garden area.
verdicts.photo_observation: Earth Pit Location (page 16) and page 13: narrow side corridor with a soil/garden strip; LA pit and DC earth pit marked in the soil next to the corridor.
verdicts.rationale: Pit location in a corridor next to a garden strip matches the description; 'west' direction is not independently verifiable from the photo.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.photo_observation: No photo of the internet router found on pages 5-19.
verdicts.rationale: Router location is not documented in the photos.

verdicts.question: What's the Wi-Fi strength of the router near to the String inverter/Envoy?
verdicts.photo_observation: No Wi-Fi signal screenshot or router photo in the report. Observations (page 20) state Wi-Fi up to the solar meter location is under customer scope.
verdicts.rationale: Wi-Fi strength cannot be verified from photos.

verdicts.question: Did you pin the site location in your WhatsApp when you were at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Report page 1 includes GPS coordinates (12.7712268, 77.6058441) and a Google Maps link; no WhatsApp screenshot in photos.
verdicts.rationale: GPS location is recorded in the report, but the WhatsApp pin itself is not photo-verifiable.

verdicts.question: What type of energy meter is currently installed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Meter Box (page 9): Schneider/L&T 'EM101+' meter labelled '1 PHASE 2 WIRE AC STATIC WATTHOUR METER', 240 V 5-30 A, with green backlit LCD display; two incoming/outgoing conductor pairs (red/blue).
verdicts.rationale: Meter nameplate and LCD clearly confirm a single-phase digital (static) meter.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9 meter photo shows the single-phase digital meter matching electrical Q1.
verdicts.rationale: Meter photo matches the stated single-phase digital meter.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 15-16: 'Main Meter' panel labelled, with the proposed AC cable (purple) route from Q Relay & Envoy through 'Solar Meter & Accessories' to the main meter.
verdicts.rationale: Termination at the main meter panel is marked in the equipment photos.

verdicts.question: Is the Termination Point easily visible or sealed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9: meter terminal block visible through a transparent terminal cover, but the cover is secured with a yellow utility seal and wire. Main meter panel on page 15 is a closed grey enclosure.
verdicts.rationale: Terminals are visible through the clear cover but the meter is sealed; whether the actual termination point is accessible without breaking a seal is unclear.

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: No existing LA visible on the roof or terrace in pages 5-12; layout (pages 17-18) shows a new LA proposed at the roof ridge and an LA pit proposed (page 16).
verdicts.rationale: Photos show no existing LA and the design proposes a new one, consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is space available for CT within Energy meter panel?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9: meter enclosure is tight around the meter with an adjacent control device; interior of the main meter panel (page 15, grey box) is not shown open.
verdicts.rationale: Panel interior space for CTs cannot be confirmed from the photos.

verdicts.question: In case of an Enphase system, is the distance between the farthest micro-inverter and IQ Gateway > 50m?
verdicts.photo_observation: Enphase IQ8P x5 on a 4.5 x 5.3 m roof (page 17); Envoy location marked next to the main meter (pages 15-16); cable route runs down the building side (pages 11-14) of a ~12 m building.
verdicts.rationale: Compact array and short documented cable route are consistent with a run well under 50 m.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 15-16: solar meter & accessories are planned in a separate location on top of an adjacent cabinet beside the main meter box; caption says removing the obstacle there is customer scope.
verdicts.rationale: Placing the solar meter outside the main meter panel is consistent with no space inside it.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available to house the Enphase accessories or ACDB components?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 15-16: Q Relay & Envoy and solar meter/accessories are marked outside the main meter panel, on the wall/cabinet next to it.
verdicts.rationale: Accessories are planned outside the main panel, consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 16 (Earth Pit Location) and page 13: open soil/garden strip alongside the side corridor with LA pit and DC earth pit marked.
verdicts.rationale: Exposed soil area for earth pits is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pits are proposed in a garden soil strip (page 16); no chamber is installed or shown yet.
verdicts.rationale: Chamber type is a design choice that is not visible in the photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Access is by a steel ladder (pages 6-7) to a steel walkway with railings and safety netting (pages 5, 7, 10), onto a sloped metal sheet roof at G+2+headroom (~12 m) with open edges (page 11).
verdicts.rationale: Railings and netting reduce risk, but ladder access to a sloped sheet roof at ~12 m with unguarded edges is a working-at-height concern; reviewer should confirm the 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is space present in rooftop to store the panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Material Storage (page 9) and page 6 bottom: covered tiled terrace under a sheet canopy with clear floor area marked for storage.
verdicts.rationale: A clear, covered, flat terrace area is available for storing panels flat.

verdicts.question: In case of sloped roof MS structure, provide the dimension of rafter to rafter, purlin
verdicts.photo_observation: Payload answer is truncated; the PDF (page 4) reads 'Purlin to Purlin is 0.90, 0.95, 0.90 and rafter to rafter is 1m'. No photo of the headroom roof's underside purlins/rafters with measurements; page 19 only measures the sheet profile pitch (0.20 m).
verdicts.rationale: Dimensions are not visually verifiable; also note the extracted designer answer is truncated relative to the PDF.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimensions for solar meter cubicle placement (L x W of wall).
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 15-16: proposed solar meter location on top of/against a cabinet beside the main meter; area currently obstructed (customer to clear). No tape measurement shown.
verdicts.rationale: 700 x 700 mm cannot be verified from the photos and the space is currently obstructed.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimension for earth pits location (L x W of available space).
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 16: long, narrow garden strip along the side corridor; proportions are consistent with ~0.75 m wide by many metres long.
verdicts.rationale: Narrow-and-long soil strip matches the stated 750 x 15000 mm proportions; exact dimensions not measured in photo.

verdicts.question: Is LAN cable under customer scope?
verdicts.photo_observation: No photo relevant. Observations (page 20) state 'Wi-Fi up to the solar meter location is under customer scope.'
verdicts.rationale: Commercial-scope question not verifiable from photos; reviewer should reconcile with the Wi-Fi customer-scope note.

verdicts.question: Is there any shadow that affects the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: A large tree stands just beyond the roof ridge and appears taller than the roof (pages 5, 10, cable-routing photo); a yellow water tank sits on the adjacent slab next to the roof (pages 5, 10; modelled west of the array on pages 17-18). No shadow analysis photo.
verdicts.rationale: Potential shading sources (tall tree, water tank) are adjacent to the array; whether they shade the panels cannot be confirmed without a shadow study.

verdicts.question: Is there any trench work to be done to carry the AC cable to the meter location?
verdicts.photo_observation: AC cable (purple) route runs over the roof, down the building wall and along the sheet canopy to the meter (pages 10-11, 14-16); caption on page 14 says a hole is to be made to run the AC cable. No below-ground run shown.
verdicts.rationale: Documented AC route is wall/canopy-mounted with no trench, consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Microinverter system (Enphase IQ8P), so no DCDB/string inverter. Routes are drawn as proposed lines: AC (purple) + earthing (green/orange) along the ridge (page 10) and down the roof edge/wall (page 11); earthing lines continue along the parapet (page 12) and down the side wall to the LA/DC pits (pages 13, 16). The purple AC line is not shown on page 12-13 and reappears at the canopy/hole on page 14, then to Q Relay & Envoy -> Solar Meter -> Main Meter (pages 15-16). No installed conduit or clipping exists yet (pre-install survey).
verdicts.rationale: Overall route is plausible, but the AC run between the roof edge (page 11) and the canopy entry point (page 14) is not traced continuously, and conduit/clipping cannot be assessed on a proposed route.
